lines.text: Ever spot the right answer, but couldn't have come up with it yourself?
That gap is recognition versus recall.
Researchers tested 392 graduates on their old high school classmates.
lines.say: Researchers tested three hundred ninety-two graduates on their old high school classmates.

lines.text: Fifteen years on, they still recognized names and faces ninety percent of the time.
But recalling names from a blank page kept fading year after year.
Picking from a list feels like knowing.
So test yourself on a blank page. If you can't recall it, you don't own it yet.

post.title: Why You Recognize Answers You Can't Remember #shorts
post.description: Recognizing the answer isn't the same as knowing it. Bahrick, Bahrick & Wittlinger (1975) found graduates still recognized classmates' names and faces about 90% of the time 15 years on, while free recall kept declining. Study tip: test yourself from a blank page. #psychology #shorts #memory #studytips
